Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application, you also need to submit the following supporting documents:
- A copy (or copies) of your official degree certificate(s) (if you have already completed your degree)
- A copy (or copies) of your official academic transcript(s), showing full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained
- Official English translations of the certificate(s) and transcript(s)
- One reference letter on headed paper
- Evidence of your English language ability (if your first language is not English)
- Any additional documents required for this programme (see Entry requirements for this programme)
- A copy of the photo page of your passport
You have **42 days** to submit your application once you begin the process. You may save and return to your application as many times as you wish to update information, complete sections or upload supporting documents such as your final transcript or your language test.
**Reference**: Please provide one reference. This should typically be an academic reference but in cases where this is not possible then a reference from a current employer may be accepted instead. Certain programmes, such as the MBA programme, may also accept an employer reference. If you already have a copy of a reference on letter headed paper then please upload this to your application. If you do not already have a reference to upload then please enter your referee’s name and contact details on the online application and we will contact your referee directly.
**Employment and Experience**: Please complete this section as fully as possible with all employments relevant to your course. Additional details may be attached in your personal statement/proposal where appropriate.

Academic Requirements.content:
Previous study of Statistics or Computing Science is not required.
Showing standard entry requirements: **2.1 Hons (or non-UK equivalent)** in a degree with a **substantial Mathematics component** (at least equivalent to Level-1 courses in Mathematics and Level-2 courses in Calculus and Linear Algebra at the University of Glasgow) with **at least 20% of credit bearing modules in University Level Mathematics at an average grade of pass**.
Accepted modules normally accepted to meet the credit bearing module requirement include: Calculus; Complex Analysis; Discrete Mathematics; Econometrics; Group Theory (Or Groups); Linear Algebra; Mathematical Analysis; Mathematics; Mechanics; Multivariate Statistical Analysis; Numerical Analysis Mathematics; Ordinary Differential Equations; Partial Differential Equations; Probability; Real Analysis; Real Variable function; Statistics; Stochastic Methods; Topology.
The mathematics component must be at least equivalent to Level-1 courses in Mathematics and Level-2 courses in Calculus and Linear Algebra at the University of Glasgow. This course is aimed at those from a maths/stats background. Those with a computing background may wish to apply for the Data Science programme instead.
China-specific academic entry requirements: **Bachelor degree at 70%/75%/80%/85%/87%** depending on university attended — see Result Required 2.1 on the China University Grade Equivalences List — in a degree with a substantial Mathematics component (at least equivalent to Level-1 courses in Mathematics and Level-2 courses in Calculus and Linear Algebra at the University of Glasgow) with at least 20% of credit bearing modules in University Level Mathematics at an average grade of pass.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
For applicants from non-English speaking countries, as defined by the [UK Government](https://www.gov.uk/student-visa/knowledge-of-english), the University sets a minimum English Language proficiency level.
- **IELTS Academic and Academic Online:** **6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. IELTS One Skill Retake accepted. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome), tests taken up to 20 January 2026:** **90 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 20; Listening 19; Speaking 19; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- **TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome), tests taken from 21 January 2026:** **92 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 22; Listening 20; Speaking 23; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- **Pearsons PTE Academic:** **65 overall** with no subtest less than Reading 60; Listening 60; Speaking 65; Writing 60. Online PTE not accepted for entry. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **Cambridge Proficiency in English (CPE) and Cambridge Advanced English (CAE):** **176 overall with no subtest less than 169**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **Oxford English Test:** **7 overall with no subtest less than 6**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **LanguageCert Academic/ Academic Online:** **70 overall with no subtest less than 65**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **Password Skills Plus:** **6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **Trinity College Integrated Skills in English II:** two subtests at **96 or higher**, and two subtests at **80 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **Kaplan Test of English:** any two subtests at **480 or higher**, and any two subtests at **450 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**.
- **University of Glasgow Pre-sessional courses:** tests are accepted for **2 years following date of successful completion**.
Alternatives to English Language qualification:
- Degree from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have studied for a minimum of their final year at Undergraduate level, or 9 months at Master's level, and must have completed their degree in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
- Undergraduate 2+2 and 3+1 degrees from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have completed their final year of study in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
For international students, the Home Office has confirmed that the University can choose to use these tests to make its own assessment of English language ability for visa applications to degree level programmes. The University is also able to accept UKVI approved Secure English Language Tests (SELT) but does not require a specific UKVI SELT for degree level programmes; it still accepts any of the English tests listed for admission to this programme.
The University of Glasgow accepts evidence of the required language level from the English for Academic Study Unit Pre-sessional courses. Pre-sessional courses give direct entry to the University programme for successful students (no need to take IELTS). More information on [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mlc/eas/pre-sessionalcourses/). The University can also consider pre-sessional courses accredited by the below BALEAP approved institutions to meet the language requirements for admission to postgraduate taught degrees: Heriot Watt; Kingston Upon Thames; Middlesex University; Manchester University; Reading University; Edinburgh University; ST Andrews University; UCL; Durham.
As part of the online application, applicants need to submit evidence of English language ability if their first language is not English. In the online application, under **English Language Proficiency**, applicants should state the date of any English language test taken (or to be taken) and the award date (or expected award date if known).

Program Overview.content:
Data Analytics MSc is offered at the University of Glasgow's Gilmorehill campus, with teaching starting in September. The MSc is **12 months full-time**; the University also offers a part-time online MSc in Data Analytics.
Data is becoming an ever increasing part of modern life, yet the talent to extract information and value from complex data is scarce. This Masters provides a thorough grounding in state-of-the art methods for learning from data, both in terms of statistical modelling and computation, and gives practical hands-on experience in carrying out various data-driven analytical projects. Previous study of Statistics or Computing Science is not required.
The Statistics Group at Glasgow is a large group, internationally renowned for its research excellence. Its expertise spans topics including biostatistics and statistical genetics; environmental statistics; statistical methodology; statistical modelling; and the scholarship of learning and teaching in statistics.
The programme works closely with [The Data Lab](http://www.thedatalab.com/), an internationally leading research and innovation centre in data science. Students benefit from learning and networking events that connect leading organisations seeking business analytics skills with students looking for opportunities in this field. The Masters in Data Analytics is accredited by the [Royal Statistical Society](https://www.rss.org.uk/).
Students are required to take 10 compulsory taught courses and select 1 taught course from the optional courses in semester 2. In the summer, students complete one project route: Statistics Project and Dissertation, or Statistics Project and Dissertation (with Placement).
Graduates have an excellent track record of gaining employment in many sectors including medical research, the pharmaceutical industry, finance and government statistical services, while others have continued to a PhD.

Financial Aid.content:

- [ScottishPower Master Scholarship](https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/scottishpowermasterscholarship/): scholarships for the 2026/27 academic year for postgraduate studies at UK universities in areas including Data / Cyber / Cyber Security / Telecoms / Business Analytics / Cloud Computing.

- [Alumni Discount](https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/alumnidiscount/): **20% tuition fee discount** to eligible self-funded University of Glasgow alumni starting a Postgraduate Taught Masters or Postgraduate Research programme in the 2026/27 academic year.

- [The Dima Alhaj Scholarship](https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/thedimaalhajscholarship/): **now closed**; offered to 1 undergraduate applicant and 1 postgraduate taught applicant joining in September 2026; not available to PhD, PGdip, PDGE or part time programmes and cannot be combined with any other University of Glasgow scholarship.

- [Glasgow Highland Society Scholarship](https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/glasgowhighlandsocietyscholarship/): multiple grants of up to **£500** for new and continuing University of Glasgow students who meet the eligibility requirements.
The scholarships above are relevant to this programme. For more funding opportunities [search the scholarships database](https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/search/#/applicant,pg,781).

Multiple Applications.content: If you are applying for more than one programme, you will need to go through this process for each programme you apply to.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
It may be possible to defer your offer to the next available intake. Deferral requests will be considered individually and are not guaranteed.
Deferral requests for the 2027 intake are open. To be considered for a deferral, you must have accepted a conditional or unconditional offer for the 2027 intake and have paid any relevant deposits to secure your place on the course. The deadline for requesting a deferral to the 2027 intake is **30 September 2026**. If you do not meet these criteria, your request will declined.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- You can apply for a postgraduate taught programme if you have not yet finished your first degree. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you finishing your degree at the required grade. If you are made a conditional offer, then you should upload your final results (transcript and degree certificate) when you receive them.
- You can normally apply for a programme if you have not yet met the English language requirements. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you meeting the English language requirements by the date stated on your offer letter. A few exceptions exist where an English test is required at time of application; applicants should check the programme page for details.
- If you cannot provide all required documents when you apply, it is still possible to apply, but you must include a full current transcript (and an English translation if required). The University may then be able to make you a conditional offer, and you can upload the remaining documents at a later date. Some programmes require all listed documents before a decision can be made.
